study_identification_part.si4_title: A neuroimaging measure to capture heterogeneous patterns of atrophy in Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract explicitly states aims to quantify heterogeneity of neurodegeneration in PD and DLB using normative modeling and to test associations between total outlier count and clinical measures, matching both hypothesis and intended purpose.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: “We aimed to quantify patterns of neurodegenerative dissimilarity in participants with PD and DLB and evaluate the potential clinical relevance of total outlier count by testing its association with key clinical measures in PD and DLB.”

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: For the recalibration controls used with the existing normative model, the paper details recruitment sources, diagnostic exclusions, age range, and that imaging was quality controlled; final control counts from each site are also reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “Structural T1w-MRI data from two sites were used. The first site at University College London (UCL), included 108 participants with PD, 36 with DLB and 38 controls… Exclusions were a history of traumatic brain injury, or major co-morbid psychiatric or confounding neurological disorders… Controls were recruited from spouses of patients and UCL volunteer databases. Inclusion criteria were being aged 50-80 and exclusions were the presence of past neurological or psychiatric history, or cognitive impairment on history or neuropsychological testing.” … “Structural T1w-MRI scans from NACC ADRC ‘8361’ were acquired on 1.5 T GE scanners… Processed images were quality controlled by visually inspecting grey and white matter boundaries… by a researcher blind to clinical status.”

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The reference normative model incorporated age and sex as covariates and accounted for site differences when modeling cortical thickness and subcortical volumes.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: “Rutherford and colleagues … modelled normative lifespan curves … using a warped Bayesian Linear Regression with age and sex as covariates, and accounting for site differences.”

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The study cites the existing normative dataset developed by Rutherford et al. and notes it comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites.”

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: MRI modality, scanner models/field strengths, and acquisition parameters for the primary data collection sites are specified.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: “Structural T1w-MRI scans at UCL were acquired on a 3 T Siemens Magnetom Prisma… parameters: 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxel, TE = 3.34 ms, TR = 2530 ms, flip angle = 7°, acquisition time = 9 min. Structural T1w-MRI scans from NACC ADRC ‘8361’ were acquired on 1.5 T GE scanners.”

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software (FreeSurfer v6.0.0) and steps (recon-all, extraction of cortical thickness and subcortical volumes) are described along with visual quality control procedures.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: “The ‘recon-all’ function in FreeSurfer v6.0.0 … was used to process all UCL and NACC MRI data. Cortical thickness values … and subcortical volumes … were extracted. Processed images were quality controlled by visually inspecting grey and white matter boundaries, and subcortical segmentation boundaries… by a researcher blind to clinical status.”

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study applied an existing normative model rather than building a new one, so internal validation of a newly built reference cohort does not apply.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “Rutherford and colleagues… modelled normative lifespan curves… Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites.”

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Because the study used an existing normative model rather than developing a new one, external validation of a newly trained model is not applicable.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “Rutherford and colleagues… modelled normative lifespan curves… Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites.”

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: Normative scores were obtained from an existing Rutherford et al. model; no new model was trained in this study, so specifying a new modeling approach is not applicable.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: “Rutherford and colleagues … modelled normative lifespan curves… Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites.”

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The study relied on a previously published normative model and did not report new performance metrics for reference model training, making this item not applicable.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “Rutherford and colleagues … modelled normative lifespan curves… Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites.”

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No new data partitioning was performed for training a reference model because an existing normative model was used.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: “Rutherford and colleagues … modelled normative lifespan curves… Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites.”

nm11_reproducibility.reason: The source of the normative model is cited and the software used to apply it, including PCNToolkit version, is specified, providing traceability to reproduce scoring.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: “Rutherford and colleagues (Rutherford et al., 2022) modelled normative lifespan curves…” and “All modelling steps were performed using PCNToolkit (v0.20) (Rutherford et al., 2022).”

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: The study reports diagnostic inclusion and exclusion criteria for PD and DLB participants at both sites and notes visual QC, with final clinical sample sizes provided, but reasons for any exclusions beyond the stated criteria are not detailed.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “They were diagnosed as having PD or probable DLB if they satisfied Queen Square Brain Bank PD diagnostic criteria… Exclusions were a history of traumatic brain injury, or major co-morbid psychiatric or confounding neurological disorders; and for participants with PD, presence of dementia was also an exclusion criterion… Controls were recruited… Inclusion criteria were being aged 50-80 and exclusions were the presence of past neurological or psychiatric history, or cognitive impairment…” and “Participants from site ‘8361’ were included if they had a structural MRI scan and met the following criteria… 1) dementia diagnosis… Lewy body disease… 4) absence of a diagnosis of PD.” plus QC: “Processed images were quality controlled by visually inspecting grey and white matter boundaries…”

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses of total outlier counts and associations adjusted for age and sex, but no additional disease-specific clinical covariates (e.g., medication status or disease duration) were modeled.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: “Linear regressions, correcting for age and sex, were used to test for group differences in total outlier count… Linear regressions adjusting for age and sex were used to test associations between total outlier count and composite cognitive score, MoCA and visuo-perception…”

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical imaging data sources are clearly identified as the UCL Vision in Parkinson’s disease study and the NACC ADRC ‘8361’ dataset.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “The first site at University College London (UCL), included 108 participants with PD, 36 with DLB and 38 controls, from the Vision in Parkinson’s disease study… The second site was the pseudoanonymised Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center (ADRC) ‘8361’ which contributes data to the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (NACC) database.”

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes and demographic/clinical descriptors such as age, sex distribution, education, disease duration, and MMSE are reported in the results table comparing PD and DLB.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: “We included 108 participants with PD (all from the UCL site); and 61 people with DLB (36 from UCL, 25 from the NACC site), plus 165 controls…” and Table 1 lists “Age… Male… Education… Disease duration… MMSE.”

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: The paper details the cognitive and disease-specific assessments (MMSE, MoCA, composite cognitive score, Hooper Visual Organisation Test, MDS-UPDRS, UM-PDHQ, HADS) and notes clinical assessments were performed the same day as MRI.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: “Clinical assessment, performed on the same day as the MRI scan, included detailed neuropsychology… Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)… Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA)… composite cognitive score… Hooper Visual Organisation Test… Disease-specific measures included the Movement Disorder Society Unified PD Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS)… UM-PDHQ… and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS).”

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores were defined as z-scores below -1.96 indicating atrophy, aggregated into total outlier counts, and clinical relevance was interpreted via associations with cognition and visuoperception.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: “Outliers were defined as z-scores < -1.96… The total number of outliers across the 169 regions… was summed per participant to provide the total outlier count.” and “Higher total outlier counts were associated with poorer MoCA… composite cognitive scores… in DLB, and visuoperception… in PD.”
